findings.problem: loadProjectAncestorIdsForRequest memoises the ancestor chain in a module-level WeakMap keyed on the object passed as 'request'. Request-scoped callers pass the Hono context or a transaction, but the websocket topic authorisation (both native topics, also run by the 60-second re-authorisation floor), loadApprovalTargetByApprovalId, loadApprovalTargetByKey when no executor is given, and pending-action read summaries (default executor db) pass the global db singleton. Entries keyed on db are never evicted (only a rejected promise is removed), so the first chain loaded for a project is reused for the life of the process: after a re-parent or an ancestor soft-delete those paths keep evaluating inherited AUTHORITY from the old ancestors (and reach in the in-memory reaches() call).
findings.impact: Stale authorisation until restart: a person who held a project grant on the OLD parent keeps that inherited role for approval decide/withdraw (hasApprovalCapability) and socket authority on the moved subtree, and newly inherited access is not seen (fail-closed). Reach on these paths is still re-checked by fresh SQL predicates (requestWorkItemScope, currentProjectReachPredicate in ws/repository.ts), which limits the leak to callers still in reach. Also an unbounded per-process cache.
findings.recommended_fix: Never memoise on db: in loadProjectAncestorIdsFor/projectAncestryFor skip the cache when request === db (or require a request/tx object), and pass a per-call object from the ws and approval paths. Add a test: load via the ws path, re-parent, load again, assert the new chain.

findings.problem: Server-side eligibility now accepts ancestor roster members (assignee-eligibility.ts:27-45), but GET /api/projects/{id}/assignable (the only picker source for properties, context menu, bulk toolbar, grouped board, create dialog) still selects membership rows with scope_id = projectId only, and the self-assign lookup at work-item/index.ts:1916-1924 is exact-project too.
findings.impact: Inherited members (PR-2: members of a parent are members of its children) are never offered in any assignee picker and cannot self-assign in a child project unless someone adds an explicit child row; the API and UI disagree.
findings.recommended_fix: Use loadProjectAncestorIds and inArray(scopeId, [projectId, ...ancestors]) in listAssignablePeople and the self-entry lookup (keep the strongest-role dedupe); add an integration test that a parent member appears in the child's /assignable.

findings.problem: Intake conversion validates the effective default assignee with a membership join on scope_id = project.id only, while project settings (resolveAssigneeEligibility) and canonical create accept ancestor roster members.
findings.impact: A parent-project member configured as the project (or request-type) default assignee is silently skipped at intake as not_a_project_member, so AS-11 behaves differently on the intake path than on create.
findings.recommended_fix: Call resolveAssigneeEligibility(tx, project.id, id) (ancestor-aware) instead of the bespoke join; add an intake test with an inherited default assignee and one that sets both defaults to prove request-type precedence (AS-12).

findings.problem: callerRankInProject (the roster rank ceiling) ignores inherited grants: with no direct grant on the child it uses the WORKSPACE role rank, while authorityFor uses the nearest ancestor's project grant. A workspace admin narrowed to project-lead on a parent can therefore grant/override child roles up to the workspace rank, including a self-override on their own inherited row (no self-edit guard), and a workspace member with an inherited lead gets a lower ceiling than their authority.
findings.impact: Inconsistent ceiling; today limited because resolveRosterRole only grants system project roles (roster.repository.ts:186), but it widens the moment another system project role above lead exists.
findings.recommended_fix: Compute the rank from the same selected grants as authorityFor (direct project grants, else nearest-ancestor grants, else workspace), and refuse edits to the caller's own row.

findings.problem: The Members tab offers every role regardless of the caller's rank (the response carries no caller rank), so the only guard is a 403; error toasts show raw server strings with code prefixes and a project UUID (e.g. 'inherited_membership: inherited from project <uuid>...', 'pending_action_target_changed'); the role Select on inherited rows silently creates an override with no explanation; the server's removable flag is ignored; empty state renders twice (:181-188 and :335-348). Composition itself matches Kaneo members-table (Table/Avatar/Select/Menu/AlertDialog, no native controls).
findings.impact: Confusing, untranslated errors and avoidable 403s on a core P1 screen; not browser-verified.
findings.recommended_fix: Return callerRank (or per-role assignable flags) and filter the Select; map error codes to i18n messages naming the parent project; label the override action on inherited rows; use removable; verify in a browser against Kaneo's workspace members screen.

findings.problem: The single-item deletion approval now shows the project and an impact section, but 'Requested by' shows the person who asked for the deletion (not the item's requester WI-23 asks about), the portal-visibility line is fixed copy shown whether or not the item is customer-visible, and the dialog says the item 'can be restored for 30 days' although no restore route or reveal filter exists (recoveryDays is a client default).
findings.impact: The approver is told the action is recoverable when it is not, and sees misleading requester/portal impact.
findings.recommended_fix: Send the item's requester and customer visibility in the summary and render them; drop or qualify the restore promise until WI-21 restore ships (P2).

findings.problem: The purge locks the parent row FOR UPDATE and then takes the project hierarchy advisory lock, while set-work-item-parent, delete and move take the advisory lock first; the comment claims serialisation with detach-parent, which takes no hierarchy lock.
findings.impact: A concurrent set-parent on the purged parent can deadlock; Postgres aborts one side (purge reports the row failed and retries next run). No data loss, but noisy failures.
findings.recommended_fix: Read project_id unlocked, take the advisory lock, then lockEligibleWorkItem and re-check the project; fix the comment.

findings.problem: Re-parenting and roster changes invalidate realtime authorisation only for the project itself; descendants whose inherited reach changed are re-checked only by the 60-second refresh floor (which, via Q1, may itself use a stale chain).
findings.impact: Up to 60 s (longer with Q1) of continued realtime events on descendant projects after a parent membership is removed or a subtree is moved.
findings.recommended_fix: Invalidate the whole descendant set (descendantProjectIds) or the workspace on these writes.

findings.problem: A bulk close of up to 500 items fires one hierarchy-children GET per item in parallel and includes already-closed items.
findings.impact: Request burst on large bulk transitions.
findings.recommended_fix: Bound concurrency (as elsewhere, 8) and skip closed items, or add a batch endpoint.

findings.problem: The Workflow page still shows the new States editor (dnd-kit) and Kaneo's ColumnEditor (native drag) as two separately reorderable lists, distinguished only by a note.
findings.impact: Two drag behaviours for related concepts on one page; needs browser judgement.
findings.recommended_fix: Decide whether columns are derived from states; if so hide the column reorder, otherwise label the relationship clearly.

findings.problem: With the new false default, the web client never sends customerVisible and no route changes visibility later, so staff files on public comments can never be shown to customers.
findings.impact: Customers cannot receive files on public replies.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a composer visibility toggle or an attachment visibility update route (P2), or record the decision.

findings.problem: Export pages now also run the row-facts and SLA decoration queries, which the CSV does not use.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an opt-out flag for the export path.
